clips.text: I'd have called it a skier too, right up until it waved back.
I counted bootprints, and now I wish I'd kept my eyes on the strap.
I'd like to believe Mara about the car, but I remember the road being closed.
I'd recognize my own hand, wouldn't I?
I've already counted two knocks; I wish they'd told me sooner.
I put that wool on before I thought to ask who'd warmed it.
I'm shorter than that sheet, and I'm still checking.
I keep looking at the dent in the bed, as if it'll tell me who slept there.
I've got my hand on the latch and no better idea than opening it.
I slept through a whole candle burning down, apparently.
I was hoping for a back door; they've given me stairs.
I can hear every step I take from underneath it.
I've come down far enough that I can't hear the wind anymore.
I keep brushing the wall; I'd rather have cold stone than lose where I am.
I'd take a mop cupboard over another room with a sheet.
I'm looking for the feet under that sheet, and I hate that I know to look.
I've barely left the door and the snow's already working into my cuffs.
I've been walking toward those lights without once seeing anything move beside them.
I've tucked my fingers into my sleeves and somehow they're still colder than my face.
I can feel a fold in my sock; of course that's what bothers me now.
I keep holding my breath to listen, then scaring myself when I let it out.
I'm trying to remember my own handwriting without looking at my hands.
I've picked a spot to stare at and now I can't stop checking it.
I should move before my knees decide this is where we're staying.
I was counting my breaths; I've stopped liking the number three.
I'd settle for someone telling me I've come to the wrong house.
